name: Dogpatch
manufacturer: Unknown — believed to originate from stolen veterinary clinic stock, repackaged by the Gray Zone distributors
description: Expired large-animal sedative (originally formulated for synthetic livestock in GLMZ's vertical farm complexes) dissolved in ethanol and cut with an over-the-counter antihistamine. Produces a heavy, dissociative sedation that the Gray Zone residents use for pain management, sleep, and escaping psychological distress. The green tint comes from the original veterinary dye still present in the expired compound.
effects: dreamless heavy sleep if taken in quantity
side_effects: respiratory depression — the leading cause of overdose death in the Gray Zone
unpredictable potency between batches due to varying expiration states
cultural_context: Dogpatch is what people take when they can't afford to feel anymore. Chronic pain from unaugmented physical labor, untreated injuries, and psychological trauma from the Gray Zone life make it ubiquitous. Street medics consider it the most dangerous drug in the Gray Zone not because of addiction but because the lethal dose varies wildly batch to batch. Some the Gray Zone communities have informal 'watchers' who sit with Dogpatch users to make sure they keep breathing.
story_hooks: A batch of Dogpatch has hit the Gray Zone with three times the normal potency — people are dying in their sleep, and someone needs to trace the supply chain before more die
A Tier 3 pharmacist has been quietly donating expired veterinary stock to a the Gray Zone clinic, not knowing it's being converted into Dogpatch downstream

A the Gray Zone watcher who has kept vigil over Dogpatch users for years is now dying of liver failure herself — her community wants to get her into a Tier 3 hospital, which will require navigating corporate healthcare bureaucracy
